provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Pet family batch. Two buyers in one category: mobile vets (licensed, regulated) and sitters and walkers. No medical advice or outcome claims anywhere; every clinical sentence is the vet's. Licence, bonding and insurance stay as bracketed placeholders. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The first visit at the owner's home, what the sitter checks (keys, alarm, feeding spot, leash, the pet's quirks), the key handoff and the signed care sheet
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners won't hand a stranger their house key without meeting them first. Booking the meet-and-greet is the real first sale.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How keys and door codes are stored, lockbox options, alarm codes, what happens to keys after the last visit, and who else ever has access to the home
pageStructurePlus.why: Pet sitting means letting someone into the house. Owners judge how keys are handled as closely as how the dog is walked.

pageStructurePlus.section: Sample visit report and GPS walk log
pageStructurePlus.contains: What each visit report includes (food, water, potty, medication given as the owner instructed, a shot of the pet), the GPS walk route, and when owners hear from the sitter
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners away from home want proof the visit happened. A sample report on the site answers that before they ask.

pageStructurePlus.section: House-call vet visit: what to expect
pageStructurePlus.contains: Which appointment types the mobile vet offers at home, what the vet brings, the space needed indoors, what is referred to a clinic or hospital, and the travel fee
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners of anxious cats, senior dogs or several pets choose a mobile vet to skip the car ride. They book once they know what can and can't happen at home.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How to request an end-of-life visit, scheduling and [after-hours availability if offered], aftercare and cremation options, what the family can expect, and a quiet contact route
pageStructurePlus.why: Families search for this at the hardest moment. A calm, plain page with a gentle way to reach the vet matters more than any other page on the site.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Peak holiday dates, overnight stays versus drop-in visits, booking deadlines, holiday surcharges and the waitlist
pageStructurePlus.why: Sitters book out over the holidays first. Owners decide on whether their dates are open and what overnights cost.

designDirections.name: Drop-In Visits
designDirections.bestFor: Solo pet sitters and dog walkers who need their area, visit prices and a meet-and-greet request
designDirections.headlineSample: Dog walking and pet sitting in {City}, right at home
designDirections.whyItFits: Teal and tangerine feel friendly and dependable, and stacked cards show walk and visit prices with the meet-and-greet request right underneath.

designDirections.name: House Call
designDirections.bestFor: Sitting and walking businesses with several staff, and mobile vets who want owners to request visits online
designDirections.headlineSample: Pet care that comes to your home in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Peach and soft rounded type feel kind and unhurried, which suits care in the owner's home, and the split hero keeps a calm pet beside the Book button.

designDirections.name: Gentle House Call
designDirections.bestFor: Mobile veterinary practices and end-of-life home visit services where trust and calm matter most
designDirections.headlineSample: Veterinary house calls in {City}, unhurried and at home
designDirections.whyItFits: Evergreen and a refined old-style serif feel like a careful practice, and a type-led hero keeps a sensitive service calm rather than cute.

openers.line: Your Maps listing for pet sitting has reviews and a phone number but no website, so an owner planning a trip can't see your visit prices or which neighbourhoods you cover.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What would sit behind that button for your pet sitting: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your mobile vet practice links to a Facebook page, and the list of house-call services lives in a pinned post. Owners of a nervous cat want that on a page they can find again.
openers.hook: Check their website field. If it's Facebook, find where services and the area are described and note how far down it sits.
openers.linkLine: Your house-call services on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your dog walking listing is an old free page with walk prices from a while back and a contact form that may not reach you. A new client who hears nothing moves on.
openers.hook: Open it and note one stale detail: old prices, a broken form, an area that changed. Never claim the form fails unless you tested it.
openers.linkLine: Same dog walking business, with a contact form that works: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your pet sitting site on my phone and the meet-and-greet form cut off halfway down. Owners look for sitters on their phone the night they book a trip.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The pet sitting site, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Booking a house call with your mobile vet service means phoning during office hours. Owners of a senior dog who can't manage the car want to request a visit at night.
openers.hook: Look for 'call to schedule' on the listing and check whether any request form exists.
openers.linkLine: A house-call request form that works after hours: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts from pet sitting visits, the cats waiting by the door and the dogs mid-walk, are the best proof of care you have, and they scroll away in days.
openers.hook: Find one recent visit or walk post you can describe exactly: the pet and the moment.
openers.linkLine: Your sitting visits on a page that stays: {demo-link}

openers.line: A Google review says you kept their elderly cat's routine exactly while they were overseas. That's what every pet owner leaving home wants to read before handing over a key.
openers.hook: Copy one phrase from a review about keys, routines, updates or an older pet. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your pet care reviews beside the booking button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Pet sitters around {City} book out over Thanksgiving and Christmas first. A holiday calendar with a waitlist fills those overnights without a dozen text threads.
openers.hook: Use this from August to October, or in February for spring break. Name the holiday.
openers.linkLine: A holiday sitting calendar with a waitlist: {demo-link}

openers.line: Owners book a last-minute work trip at 10pm and need a pet sitter by morning. If your sitting service only answers by phone, they find someone who answers online.
openers.hook: Look for comments or posts about last-minute sits, or 'text me for availability' in the bio.
openers.linkLine: A sitting request that works at 10pm: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring dog walkers. Applicants check whether a pet sitting business looks organised and insured before they apply, and so do the owners they'll walk for.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring notice or a 'join our team' story. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A pet care site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your mobile vet service covers several towns, but nobody can tell whether you drive to their side of {City} or what the travel fee is before they call.
openers.hook: Check the listing and posts for towns served or a travel fee. If neither appears, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Your house-call area and travel fees on a map: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your weekday dog walking clients pay walk by walk. A monthly walk package on the site would lock in their schedule and steady your income through the slow weeks.
openers.hook: Check their prices for packages, punch cards or monthly plans. If there are none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A monthly dog walking package page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Owners handing a pet sitter their house key want to see bonding, insurance and a background check. None of that shows on your listing.
openers.hook: Check whether they post insurance, bonding or a background check anywhere. Never invent one; the demo uses bracketed placeholders.
openers.linkLine: Your bonding, insurance and key policy, shown plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your house-call vet work comes mostly from clinic referrals. Families who search for a mobile vet themselves should be able to find you too.
openers.hook: Look for 'referred by' in reviews or thank-you posts to clinics.
openers.linkLine: Where a family searching for a mobile vet would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted shows how much care goes into each visit. A pet owner deciding who gets their house key wants to see exactly that.
openers.hook: Pick their newest visit, walk or house-call post and name it exactly: the pet and what happened. Never mention a medical detail.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted shows real care.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} where an owner could check your area and request a visit, and only found the social pages. I put together a sample with your visit types, a meet-and-greet or house-call request and a plain key and home policy, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got lost between visits. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has your service area with travel fees, a visit request that works at night and a sample visit report so owners know what they'll hear while they're away. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for pet sitters, dog walkers and mobile vets here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss when you're on the road between homes. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with your service area, a visit request form and your key policy, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link to look at tonight?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a pet care business like yours I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes between visits this week?"

IF A VET ASKS ABOUT CLINICAL WORDING:
"Nothing clinical goes on the site unless you write or approve it. I handle the logistics: area, booking and what to expect."

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.handler: "Then the site is for the holidays and for choosing new clients. A waitlist and a clear meet-and-greet step mean the next key you take is from someone you want to work with."

objections.objection: My clients find me on Nextdoor.
objections.handler: "Nextdoor finds them. The site is where they check your area, read your key policy and request a meet-and-greet without waiting on a reply to a post."

objections.objection: I'm already on a sitting app.
objections.handler: "Keep it if it brings new work. The site is where your repeat clients book you directly, so the app's cut isn't taken from regulars who already know you."

objections.objection: As a vet I have to be careful what I say online.
objections.handler: "Agreed, and the site gives no medical advice. It covers house-call logistics, the area and how to request a visit, and every clinical sentence is yours to write or approve."

objections.objection: I don't want strangers knowing I hold keys.
objections.handler: "The site never lists clients or addresses. It explains your key policy in general terms, which is what makes owners comfortable handing one over."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a service-area map, a visit request and your policies. A few weeks of regular dog walks or a handful of house calls covers it."

email.subject: Pet care site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for pet sitters and mobile vets in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll text you the link so you can look between visits. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} pet care demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, holiday travel is coming, and the pet sitters with a holiday calendar online are filling their overnights first. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a few weeks of visits, not one client's month. Sitters and walkers earn per visit, and the build has to match.
Mobile vet practices carry more budget than solo sitters. Quote the vet toward the top of the range and the solo walker toward the bottom.
Price the service-area map by towns and travel-fee zones, not by page count.
The meet-and-greet and key policy pages are their own line. They decide whether an owner hands over a key.
Keep monthly add-ons under the price of a week of daily walks. Anything higher gets cancelled in a quiet month.
For veterinary pages, budget review time with the vet: every clinical sentence is theirs, and nothing is written as advice.

lineItems.description: Max with several towns, fee zones looked up by ZIP and separate areas for walks and house calls.
Max with a full care sheet (feeding, medication as instructed, vet contact, home quirks) and an e-signature.

lineItems.item: Key and home security policy page
lineItems.description: Max when it covers lockboxes, alarm codes, key return and a [bonding and insurance] placeholder block.

lineItems.item: House-call services page for a mobile vet
lineItems.description: Max when it covers each visit type, space needed at home and what gets referred, all reviewed by the vet.

lineItems.item: End-of-life visit page with a quiet contact route
lineItems.description: Max with aftercare options, a separate gentle request form and after-hours wording supplied by the vet.
Max with several peak periods, overnight versus drop-in options and a deposit step.
Max when the care sheet, key policy and visit request are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Walks and visits photo session
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Half a day following real dog walks and drop-in visits, owners' OK on file, gives the site pets that actually look cared for at home."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on a day with several clients who agree to their pets being featured. Never photograph house numbers or keys.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the pet care business
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Weekly walk and visit posts and a current service area on your Google profile, so owners searching for a pet sitter nearby see you're active."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each sitting job
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The day the owner gets home, they get a short text asking how the sitting went, while they're still relieved the pets are fine."

whatElseYouSell.name: Holiday sitting campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Overnight sitting slots over Thanksgiving and Christmas go first. Ads that start in August get each one booked with a deposit before the rush."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in July, run August to October.

whatElseYouSell.name: Summer travel and spring break sitting push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Spring break sitters get booked the same night as the flights. A February ad to pet owners nearby puts your name in front of them that week."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in January, run February to April.

whatElseYouSell.name: Car magnet and walking bag artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A car magnet and a walking bag with your booking code, so the neighbours who see you on every dog walk know how to book you."

whatElseYouSell.name: Referral cards for groomers and pet stores
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A small card with your pet sitting or house-call booking code for the groomer's counter and the pet store's checkout."

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly pet care post planning
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "You do the walks and visits, I plan the month of posts around open slots, holiday dates and seasonal pet care reminders the vet approves."

withoutAI.route: The clinic that refers house calls
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The clinic that sends you house calls for patients who can't travel has a site that never mentions home visits. You can introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Clinics and mobile vets share patients, and the mobile vet's word gets you past the practice manager.

withoutAI.route: The pet aftercare and cremation provider
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The aftercare provider you work with for end-of-life home visits needs a calm site where families can arrange memorials and pick-up."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Aftercare providers depend on vet referrals and need a site that treats grieving families gently.

withoutAI.route: The groomer who shares the sitter's clients
withoutAI.whoPays: The groomer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The groomer whose appointments you drive dogs to between walks needs a booking-first grooming site of their own."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Walkers and groomers share the same owners and the same calendar. The introduction is a chat at the counter.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each sitter, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The pet sitter who takes your overflow at Christmas needs the same meet-and-greet and key policy pages."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Sitters trade overflow with a few peers they trust, and each has seen the site working.

withoutAI.route: Apartment buildings where the walker has many dogs
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The building where you walk five dogs a day needs a resident pet page with its pet rules and a list of approved dog walkers."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Property managers want pet-owning residents happy, and the walker is already a familiar face at the front desk.

withoutAI.route: The boarding kennel that sends overflow
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The kennel that sends you cats and senior dogs who do better at home needs a holiday boarding page of its own."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Kennels and sitters split the same holiday demand. Each refers what the other handles better.

withAI.route: Logistics phone line for the referring clinic
withAI.pitchLine: "The clinic that refers your house calls fields evening calls about refill pick-up and opening times. A logistics line answers those and reads out the emergency hospital number for anything urgent."
withAI.whyItWorks: It never answers a medical question, which is exactly what lets a practice sign off on it.

withAI.route: Memorial page writer for the aftercare provider
withAI.pitchLine: "Families share a few memories of their pet, and a gentle memorial page draft comes back for them to edit and keep."
withAI.whyItWorks: Aftercare providers want to offer comfort, not paperwork. A memorial page is a service families remember.

withAI.route: Overflow matcher for the sitter network
withAI.pitchLine: "When a pet sitting request comes in for dates you're full, it goes to the trusted sitter whose area and pets fit best."
withAI.whyItWorks: Every sitter turns work away at the holidays. Passing it to a trusted peer keeps the owner's goodwill.

withAI.route: Pet rule and walker finder for the condo board
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents ask the condo office about pet limits and who walks dogs in the building. An assistant answers from the bylaws and lists the approved dog walkers."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards field the same pet questions weekly, and the walker stays the named recommendation.

withAI.pitchLine: "The groomer you drive dogs to sends rebooking reminders drafted from each dog's last visit, and your walk pick-up gets added to the note."
withAI.whyItWorks: Groomers want full books, and the walker becomes part of every reminder.

withAI.route: Cat-friendly stay advisor for the kennel
withAI.pitchLine: "Owners answer a few questions about their cat or senior dog, and the kennel's site suggests a suite or an in-home sitter partner."
withAI.whyItWorks: Kennels lose bookings from owners who worry about stress. Offering a sitter partner keeps them in the kennel's circle.

softwareAI.name: Arrival and departure texts for each visit
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners get a text when the pet sitter arrives and leaves, so nobody on a beach wonders whether the cat got fed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the visit calendar and a phone check-in habit for each sitter.

softwareAI.name: Holiday deposit and cancellation rule for sits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Holiday pet sitting takes a deposit at booking, so a cancelled Christmas overnight doesn't cost you the clients you turned away."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build, or by August before the holidays. Needs their cancellation policy and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Pet care DM and text responder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'Do you cover my street' and 'are you free over Thanksgiving' get answered from your real area and calendar, with the meet-and-greet link. Health questions always go to the vet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the service area, prices and calendar access. It never answers health questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Client care sheets with key and alarm notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Feeding amounts, owner-instructed medication times, the vet's number and the alarm code stored securely per home, so any sitter covering a visit has it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their current care sheets and a rule for who can see key and alarm details.

softwareAI.name: Visit reports with GPS walk logs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each visit ends with a report to the owner: food, water, potty, the walk route and a shot of the pet at home."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a phone app habit for each walker and the owner's OK to receive texts.

softwareAI.name: Visit report writer from sitter notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The sitter taps a few words after each visit, and a warm note for the owner comes back ready to send, in the pet sitting business's own voice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, after visit reports are running. Needs a few sample notes they like. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Walker and sitter route scheduling
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Dog walks and drop-in visits grouped by street and time window, so each walker drives less and nobody's midday walk runs late."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once there's more than one walker. Needs client addresses, visit windows and staff availability.

softwareAI.name: Pet care phone receptionist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "With a leash in one hand and keys in the other, the pet care line still gets answered: area, prices and a visit request taken, with urgent callers given the emergency hospital number."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs area, prices and calendar access; it gives no medical advice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Monthly dog walking packages and billing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Weekday dog walking billed as a monthly package, with skipped days credited, so regulars stop paying walk by walk."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the packages they want to sell and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: House-call recall reminders from the vet's own schedule
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the mobile vet's own records say a pet is due for a visit, the owner gets a reminder with a house-call request link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, mobile vets only. Needs the due dates the vet already sets; the reminder wording is the vet's.

softwareAI.name: House-call request summary for the vet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A long house-call request becomes a short note for the mobile vet: which pet, the owner's stated reason, the address, parking and access. It never suggests a diagnosis."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, mobile vets only. Needs the request form live and the vet's approval of the summary format. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: House-call route and travel-fee calculator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The mobile vet sees the day's house calls in driving order, and owners see the travel fee for their address before they request a visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, mobile vets only. Needs fee zones and a typical day's visit list.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for pet care reviews
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each pet sitting or house-call review gets a reply drafted that thanks the family and names their pet, with no health details, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Staff bonding, insurance and background check tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every walker's background check, insurance certificate and renewal date in one place, so the pet care business can show owners it's current."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once there's staff. Needs their current documents and renewal dates.

softwareAI.name: Next-trip sitting nudge for past clients
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners who used your pet sitting at spring break get a note before summer travel, so you're the first sitter they book."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past sit dates from the calendar.

softwareAI.name: Caption writer for walk and visit posts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Post a shot from today's dog walk, and a caption in your voice, with no address or client detail, is ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs a few of their past captions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sitter payroll and visit-count report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each walker's visits, walk minutes and mileage totalled at the end of the pay period, without rebuilding it from texts."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for businesses with staff. Needs their pay rules and visit data.

softwareAI.name: New walker onboarding assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New dog walkers ask the business's own handbook about key rules, leash rules and what to do if a pet won't eat, instead of calling the owner mid-visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their written procedures and the owner's approval of every answer; anything health-related says to call the client's vet. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Client portal for visit history and invoices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners log in to see every pet sitting visit, report and invoice, and book the next walk without a text."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs visit records and invoicing in one place.

softwareAI.name: Last-minute sit matcher
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A last-minute pet sitting request goes to the staff sitter whose route, schedule and known pets fit, and the owner hears back within the evening."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs staff availability and client history. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise care sheets and visit reports for solo sitters
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built care sheets and visit reports for one pet sitting business. Every solo sitter keeps alarm codes in their notes app."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the workflow. Solo sitters are many and gather in a few online groups.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Franchise owners each cover a patch of town. A shared pet sitting template with a per-territory area map and meet-and-greet form gets every new sitter online fast."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many territories on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Professional pet sitter association member toolkit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member pet sitters a ready site with the key policy, care sheet and holiday calendar built in as a member benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewals and practical benefits. One deal reaches many sitters who trust the association.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Mobile vet vehicle outfitters' launch pack
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every vet who buys a fitted-out house-call vehicle from you needs a site with a service area and a visit request on day one."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Outfitters sell on how fast a new mobile practice starts earning. A ready launch pack is an easy line on a big invoice.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Owners search for a mobile vet by town. One network site that routes each request to the right house-call vet fills every member's calendar."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Independent mobile vets band together for coverage and need one place owners can find them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label pet sitter template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency picks up a pet sitter or dog walker now and then. License my template with the key policy and meet-and-greet request built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the part you've already built and run.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Pet care businesses an hour outside {City}
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New pet care clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one pet sitting business per side of {City}. Sitters and mobile vets an hour away don't share your clients, so the build travels."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the finished pet care proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your pet sitting booking and never connected the care sheet. I've done that setup for another sitter and can finish yours."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Owners with a stalled setup have already decided to buy. They need someone who has done it before.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Apartment developers' resident pet care partner pages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your pet-friendly buildings promise residents easy dog walking and pet care. A partner page with vetted walkers and sitters by building makes that true."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Developers market pet amenities and need trusted partners behind them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Families ask your aftercare service for a vet who does home visits. A directory of partner mobile vets by area answers them gently."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Aftercare providers serve many vets across a region and want families pointed to trusted ones.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The veterinary school's career office, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Graduates starting a mobile vet practice need a service area, a house-call request and a plain what-to-expect page. A kit for each class is a career service."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Career offices want practical launch help for graduates, and the kit is a recurring contract.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Senior living communities with resident pets
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents with pets need help with dog walks and house-call vet visits. A resident pet care page with approved providers takes it off the front desk."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Senior communities allow pets but can't staff their care. A trusted provider list is a real resident benefit.

upsellLadder.offer: Pet care site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "Pet sitting site and care plan on one contract, so a new town or a holiday rate goes up the day you text me."

upsellLadder.offer: Holiday deposit and cancellation rule for sits
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a holiday sit cancelled after they turned other clients away.
upsellLadder.line: "That cancelled Christmas sit is exactly what a pet sitting deposit protects."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests after each sitting job
upsellLadder.trigger: The site has been live a month and several sits have finished.
upsellLadder.line: "Your pet sitting clients just came home to happy pets. Let's ask them to say so."

upsellLadder.offer: Visit reports with GPS walk logs
upsellLadder.trigger: An owner texts mid-trip asking whether a visit happened.
upsellLadder.line: "A report after every visit answers 'did the dog get walked' before anyone asks."

upsellLadder.trigger: They hire a second walker or sitter.
upsellLadder.line: "Two dog walkers means two routes. Let's plan them before the midday walks start running late."

upsellLadder.trigger: It's late summer and the holiday sitting calendar still has open dates.
upsellLadder.line: "The holiday pet sitting dates are still open. A push now fills them with deposits."

upsellLadder.offer: Introduction to the clinic that refers house calls
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a clinic that sends them house-call or sitting clients.
upsellLadder.line: "The clinic that sends you pets has a site that never mentions home visits. Would you introduce me?"
